column3: Energize your décor with the sleek Viscount Side Chair. Designed with a minimalist chic form and progressive feel, Viscount comes densely padded in foam, finely upholstered in polyester fabric, and supported by tapered wood legs coated black. From the sheer force of the design to the exceptional versatility of the uses, Viscount is perfect for modern contemporary décors seeking a bold chair that makes a statement.
column4:
Tournai, on the river Scheldt in western Belgium, was one of the great tapestry towns of fifteenth-century Europe, its looms weaving hangings for dukes and churches. Cloth has sat at the heart of Belgian rooms ever since, and a well-dressed chair is its everyday descendant.

This one is all clean line. The back rises tall and narrow, curves forward to cradle the shoulders, then flares gently at the sides where it meets the seat. Dense foam sits under closely fitted woven fabric, and the seat cushion is edged with a welt, a corded seam that crisps the outline. Four tapered legs in a black finish splay slightly for a steady stance.

Pull the pair up to a round pedestal table in a city kitchen, or set them at either end of a long farmhouse table. One makes a good desk chair in a study. Dress the table in white linen, add a jug of tulips, and let the fabric bring the colour. This listing is for a set of two chairs.

column3: Revitalize your dining decor with the Viscount Dining Chairs - Set of 2. Graceful, minimalist lines blend seamlessly with the lush comfort of Viscount which features soft, stain-resistant performance velvet upholstery, dense foam padding, and black rubberwood tapered legs. Viscount's versatile vintage modern style make this set ideally suited for a variety of rooms. Place Viscount in the dining room or kitchen as dining chairs, or in the living room, entryway, or bedroom as accent chairs. This modern accent dining chair supports up to 300 lbs. and includes non-marking foot caps to protect flooring.
column4:
Long before it covered chairs, velvet was a luxury cloth traded through the great markets of Flanders, where Bruges merchants dealt in Italian silks. Set on a slim modern dining chair, it still brings a sense of occasion to the table.

The tall back narrows at the top, curves round to hold the shoulders and flares where it meets the seat. Dense foam sits beneath a performance velvet, a hard-wearing pile that resists stains, so a splash of wine at dinner can be blotted away. The tapered hardwood legs are finished in black, and non-marking caps protect the floor.

Set the pair at a dining table for dinner parties, or split them up, with one at a writing desk and the other in the hall as a place to pull on boots. The velvet glows against dark wood, brass candlesticks and a deep green wall. This listing is for a set of two chairs.

column3: With its rounded seat and open backrest, the Marsha Dining Chair Set of 2 brings a fresh take on retro dining. Upholstered in slub weave linen-like fabric, these upholstered dining chairs feature rounded padded seats and a curved open backrest that gives the set a light, vintage-inspired feel. Rubberwood legs add warmth and sturdy support, while the open-back design keeps the profile clean around a dining table, kitchen table, breakfast nook, or small seating area. Adjustable foot pins help protect flooring and keep each chair steady on uneven surfaces. Crafted with a rubberwood frame, foam padding, and linen-like fabric upholstery, this dining chair set supports up to 300 lbs. Assembly required.
column4:
Durbuy, in the wooded Belgian Ardennes, likes to call itself the smallest town in the world, and the forests around it have fed generations of country joiners. Later designers kept that respect for plain timber while giving it softer, rounder shapes.

A round, thickly padded seat sits within a frame of square hardwood posts in a natural finish, and a curved, upholstered back rests on the rear pair, leaving an opening beneath so the chair looks light. The covering is a slub weave, a fabric spun from uneven yarn for a soft, nubby texture with the look of linen. Adjustable foot pins steady each leg on an uneven floor, and some assembly is needed.

Gather them round a pedestal table in a breakfast nook, or line them along a kitchen table for weekday suppers. Pale wood and nubby cloth sit well with a jute rug, stoneware bowls and a bunch of eucalyptus. This listing is for a set of two chairs.

column3: The Anelle Dining Chair Set of 2 adds soft retro style to dining rooms, kitchens, and breakfast nooks. Upholstered in slub weave linen-like fabric, these armless dining chairs feature a curved barrel-style backrest and padded seat for a comfortable, tailored look around the dining table. Tapered wood legs add warmth and a mid-century inspired feel, while the open armless design makes each chair easy to place in smaller dining spaces or styled as an accent chair in a living room or bedroom. Protective foot pins help guard flooring from marks and scratches, making this upholstered dining chair set a practical choice for everyday meals, casual hosting, and relaxed seating. Assembly required. Weight capacity of each fabric chair: 300 lbs.
column4:
Eighteenth-century French chairmakers loved a back that followed the body, and the cabriolet, a chair whose back is hollowed into a gentle curve, became a fixture of manor and town house alike. The shape suits an old stone house in a Burgundy village such as Flavigny as well as a new apartment.

This armless version carries the idea in a fully upholstered barrel back, a rounded shell that curves forward to wrap the sitter. It is covered in a slub weave, a fabric with uneven yarns that gives a soft texture with the look of linen, and set on four tapered wood legs in a dark brown finish. Foot pins guard the floor, and assembly is needed.

The armless shape tucks neatly round a breakfast table by the window. One makes a fine accent chair in a bedroom. Set them around a dark wood table with a linen runner, a bowl of pears and a pair of tall candles. This listing is for a set of two chairs.

column3: The Anelle Dining Chair Set of 2 adds soft retro style to dining rooms, kitchens, and breakfast nooks. Upholstered in slub weave linen-like fabric, these armless dining chairs feature a curved barrel-style backrest and padded seat for a comfortable, tailored look around the dining table. Tapered wood legs add warmth and a mid-century inspired feel, while the open armless design makes each chair easy to place in smaller dining spaces or styled as an accent chair in a living room or bedroom. Protective foot pins help guard flooring from marks and scratches, making this upholstered dining chair set a practical choice for everyday meals, casual hosting, and relaxed seating. Assembly required. Weight capacity of each fabric chair: 300 lbs.
column4:
Eighteenth-century French chairmakers loved a back that followed the body, and the cabriolet, a chair whose back is hollowed into a gentle curve, became a fixture of manor and town house alike. The shape suits an old stone house in a Burgundy village such as Flavigny as well as a new apartment.

This armless version carries the idea in a fully upholstered barrel back, a rounded shell that curves forward to wrap the sitter. It is covered in a slub weave, a fabric with uneven yarns that gives a soft texture with the look of linen, and set on four tapered wood legs in a dark brown finish. Foot pins guard the floor, and assembly is needed.

The armless shape tucks neatly round a breakfast table by the window. One makes a fine accent chair in a bedroom. Set them around a dark wood table with a linen runner, a bowl of pears and a pair of tall candles. This listing is for a set of two chairs.

column3: Bring understated elegance and tailored comfort to your dining space with the Mauden Dining Chairs Set of 2. Defined by its softly curved silhouette and thoughtfully exposed back frame, this upholstered dining chair blends timeless craftsmanship with relaxed contemporary style. Upholstered in soft performance velvet, Mauden introduces rich texture and elevated comfort to dining rooms, breakfast nooks, and casual gathering spaces. The removable back cushion adds layered comfort while highlighting the chair’s distinctive open wood frame design. A generously padded seat and supportive back create a comfortable dining experience for everyday meals and extended gatherings alike. Fully assembled and crafted with a sturdy rubberwood frame, this dining chair set offers a polished yet approachable look suited for coastal, transitional, farmhouse, and modern interiors. Weight Capacity: 300 lbs.
column4:
In the farmhouses of northern France, the everyday dining chair was a joiner's piece: square posts, low rails bracing the legs, and a back left open to show its frame. Gerberoy, a timber-framed village in Picardy famous for its roses, is the sort of place such chairs belong.

Two posts rise from the back legs, finished with small rounded tops, and between them hangs a padded back cushion that lifts away, so the open timber shows. The seat is deeply padded and covered, like the back, in a performance velvet with a soft, deep pile, on a hardwood frame in a natural finish. Each chair arrives ready to use, with nothing to assemble.

Set the pair at a round table in a breakfast nook, or at the ends of a long kitchen table for Sunday lunch. Pale wood and velvet look warm with a scrubbed pine table, a jute rug and a stoneware jug of garden roses. This listing is for a set of two chairs.

Colour: Chocolate Brown as Truffle; Taupe as Fawn (photos read mid khaki tan, per the Como precedent).
Seat height 17.5 in and seat depth 16.5 in from Modway's seating dimensions.

column4:
Ticking began as the tightly woven, narrow-striped cloth that covered mattresses and pillows in country houses across France and Belgium, its dense weave made to keep the feathers in. Later generations liked it so well that they brought it out of the bedroom and onto chairs and cushions.

Here a fine woven stripe dresses a chair built like an old joiner's piece. Square back posts with small rounded tops hold a padded cushion that lifts off, leaving the timber frame open behind it. The seat is generously padded and low rails keep the natural hardwood frame firm and square. It comes ready to use, with nothing to assemble.

Bring them to a farmhouse table in a kitchen with open shelves, or a round table in a sunroom. The stripe looks crisp beside whitewashed walls, blue and white china and a bunch of lavender. This listing is for a set of two chairs.

column3: Bring relaxed sophistication to your dining space with the Aster Dining Chairs Set of 2. Defined by a tailored slipcovered silhouette and premium checked upholstery, these upholstered dining chairs add warmth and texture to both casual and formal settings. The windowpane pattern gives these parsons dining chairs a refined, timeless look, while the gently curved high back creates a comfortable seat for everyday meals and gatherings. Upholstered in a cotton linen blend fabric with polyester for durability, these slipcovered side chairs offer a soft textile and easy-care practicality. The removable slipcover is spot cleanable, making these dining room chairs especially well suited for busy households. Dense foam padding, a sturdy solid wood frame, and reinforced stretcher bars provide lasting support and stability. Whether styled around a dining table, breakfast nook, or used as accent seating, the Aster slipcovered dining chair set delivers comfort with an elevated, relaxed look. Fabric Content: 71% Polyester, 13% Acrylic, 7% Cotton, 9% Linen. Assembly required. Weight Capacity: 300 lbs.
column4:
In old French houses the best chairs were dressed for summer. Loose covers of cotton or linen went on to keep sun and dust off the upholstery, and their relaxed, tailored drape has never gone out of style. Auvers, the Oise village beloved of open-air painters, has that same easy charm.

This is a parsons chair, a clean-lined, fully upholstered side chair, with a softly curved tall back and a slipcover that falls almost to the floor. The cloth, with cotton and linen in the blend, is woven in a windowpane check: fine lines crossing to form large squares. The slipcover is removable and spot cleans. Beneath it are dense foam and a solid wood frame braced by low rails, and assembly is needed.

Set the pair at either end of a long dining table, or tuck them into a breakfast nook. Windowpane check looks at home with scrubbed oak, ironstone platters, a striped rug and armfuls of hydrangeas. This listing is for a set of two chairs.
column5:
Family: Auvers (alternates: Moret, Pontoise). Village on the Oise near Paris; the hook is French summer loose covers, kept general.
Colour: Hemp Windowpane Check as Sand Windowpane Check; Denim Windowpane Check as Navy Windowpane Check; Artichoke Windowpane Check as Fern Windowpane Check.
Name avoids "Linen" because the fabric is only 9% linen (71% polyester).
Seat height 20 in and seat depth 18 in from Modway's seating dimensions.
Cost $238.25 from the Modway trade portal 30 Oct; retail by the house pricing model.
Care: Modway says only that the removable slipcover is spot cleanable, with no cleaning code; care says spot clean only and does not say the cover can be washed.

column3: The Daven Upholstered Dining Chair combines mid-century modern style with supportive comfort in a sleek, versatile design. column4:
In 1930s Paris, the decorator Jean-Michel Frank pared the armchair down to a few strong, squared volumes covered in plain cloth or leather, and the blocky upholstered chair became a modern classic. The shape still looks fresh beside old stone and beams, as in the medieval houses of Provins, east of Paris.

This dining armchair is upholstered all over, its arms dropping straight to the floor as broad, squared legs, so it reads as one sculpted form. Under the heathered woven cover sit dense foam and a webbed seat, a lattice of strong bands that gives a little beneath you. A bracket holds the back firm, discreet glides protect the floor, and assembly is needed.

Place it at the head of a dining table to anchor a run of side chairs, or use it as a desk chair in a study. Pair it with a pale oak table, linen curtains, a ceramic lamp and a stack of art books. This listing is for one chair.

Italian furniture makers of the 1960s and 1970s, working with new moulded foams and stretch upholstery, began to treat a chair as one continuous line rather than a kit of parts. The lakes and workshop towns north of Milan were the heart of that work, and its looping, sculptural shapes still look modern today.

Here a single band of upholstery rises from the back legs, curls round behind you and comes forward to form both arms, leaving an opening at the back that keeps the chair light. The seat is deep and well padded with foam, and the velvet is a performance weave that resists stains, so a dropped forkful of sauce blots away. Non-marking pins protect the floor, and the chairs need only a little assembly.

Set the pair at a round pedestal table in a breakfast nook, or at the ends of a long dining table. Velvet loves candlelight, brass and a bowl of late figs. This listing is for a set of two chairs.

The back is a single upholstered sweep that curls forward into low arms, open at the rear so it never looks bulky. The seat is thickly cushioned and covered in a slub weave, a fabric with slightly irregular yarns that gives a soft, textured look. Underneath, a black powder-coated base rolls on smooth casters, a gas lift raises or lowers the seat, and tilt tension sets how the chair rocks back. It needs only light assembly.

Roll it up to a writing desk in a home office or a bedroom vanity where it doubles as a dressing chair. It sits happily beside a walnut desk, a brass task lamp and a framed print.

column3: Embrace the perfect blend of modern style and versatile functionality with the Oslo Barrel Dining Chair. Fully upholstered in soft textured fabric with captivating depth, the Oslo Accent Chair is as inviting as it is stylish. The barrel-shaped curved back and padded seat offer ergonomic comfort, making it an ideal choice for long meals, work sessions, or relaxation. Better for you and the environment, the upholstery fabric is also OEKO-TEX® STANDARD 100 certified. Supported by a durable metal frame hidden beneath the luxurious fabric, this versatile upholstered chair is as sturdy as it is sleek. Equipped with non-marking floor glides and arriving fully assembled, the 3-leg chair effortlessly enhances any modern dining room, kitchen, or living space. Weight Capacity: 300 lbs.
column4:
Ticino, the Italian-speaking corner of Switzerland around Lugano and Ascona, became known in the 1970s for architects who built in bold, solid geometric forms. This chair has the same quality: it reads more like a small piece of sculpture than a chair.

The back curves round in one thick, rounded band and drops to the floor as three broad legs, two at the front and one behind, with the seat set between them. A metal frame hidden inside keeps it strong, padding makes the seat and back comfortable through a long meal, and the textured weave has real depth of colour. The fabric holds OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certification, meaning it has been tested for harmful substances. It sits on non-marking glides and comes fully assembled.

Pull a pair up to a long oak dining table, or use one as a desk chair or a bedroom accent chair. Its chunky, sculpted form suits plaster walls, a jute rug, a stoneware lamp and a branch of olive. This listing is for one chair.

column4:
In the 1930s, as Metro-land spread out along the railway from London to towns like Amersham, new houses filled with three-piece suites whose rounded arms swept back into the frame. The style borrowed its curves from the picture palaces of the day, and velvet was its favourite cloth.

This sofa keeps that unbroken sweep. The back wraps round in one continuous line and curls down into the arms, so it looks finished from every side. It is covered in a performance velvet with a soft, close pile that copes with everyday spills better than a traditional velvet, and one long seat cushion takes three people. It is built for everyday family use and needs only light assembly.

Float it in an open living room facing the fire, or set it along a wall in an apartment where a bulkier sofa would crowd the floor. Pile it with linen and wool cushions, add a round stone coffee table and a brass floor lamp, and let the velvet catch the evening light.

column3: The Ingot Side Table has a solid metal body with smooth sides that taper toward a narrower base, finished in warm brass powder coat. The 16-inch round top stands 18 inches high, sized to tuck in beside a sofa or armchair. The solid body keeps a tidy footprint and wipes down with a soft cloth. column4:
Brass was first made in Britain at Tintern, in the Wye valley, in the sixteenth century, and the metal soon reached hearths across the country as candlesticks, fenders and coal scuttles. A warm gleam of gold beside a chair is about as old a comfort as an English room has.

This small table takes a simple, solid form: a round drum whose smooth sides narrow gently toward the floor. It is metal throughout, coated in a gold-toned powder finish that gives the glow of polished brass with none of the polishing. Sturdy enough for a heavy lamp or a stack of books, it comes ready to use with nothing to put together.

Set it beside a reading chair for a cup of tea and a paperback, or at the end of a sofa to hold a lamp and a dish of keys. It works as a bedside table in a guest room, and two side by side make an easy coffee table. It glows against deep green walls, dark velvet and natural linen.

column4:
Wales has spun and woven its own wool for centuries, and the Pembrokeshire mill near Solva still makes thick, nubbly cloth on working looms. Bouclé, a yarn twisted into small loops so the fabric feels like fleece under the hand, carries that same warmth into a modern room.

This armless chair is upholstered all over in a bouclé with a fine lattice texture. The seat flows straight on into broad upholstered sides that reach the floor like a pair of sled runners, and a low back curves round to hold you. Its 31-inch-wide seat leaves room to sit crosswise or with your feet tucked under. A solid wood frame padded with dense foam keeps it supportive, clear pins under the sides protect the floor, and it comes ready to use.

Put it in a bedroom corner with a lamp, by the fire in a snug, or at a desk where arms would be in the way. It sits well with sheepskin and warm oak. This listing is for one chair.

column4:
British sitting rooms of the late 1960s and 1970s loved a low, rounded chair, its upholstery swelling like one big cushion and trimmed with a polished strip of timber. The look was part comfort and part showpiece, and it has come back for good reason: few shapes are so easy to sink into.

This chair is covered in a performance velvet that shrugs off the knocks of a busy household and lifts most marks with a spot clean. The seat and back are deep and rounded, padded with layered foam for long, lazy lounging. On each side a curved band of wood is set into the upholstery, sweeping down to meet a low wooden plinth beneath. It arrives assembled, ready for its first evening.

Use it in a living room opposite the sofa, in a bedroom beside a good lamp, or as the one statement piece in a wide hallway. It loves rich company: a burl-fronted sideboard, a cream rug, brass candlesticks and a pile of design books.

This armless chair is covered in a performance fleece with a short, soft pile, stitched into rounded channels, long padded ribs that run across the back and down the length of the seat. Where the seat channels meet the front they finish in a gentle scalloped edge. The seat sits deep and close to the floor, built up with layered foam for curling up. It comes fully assembled, so it is ready to use at once.

Set it in a living room beside a low table, in a bedroom by the window, or in a den for film nights. It looks good with a striped rug, a ceramic lamp and dark wood, and it invites a blanket and a cup of tea.

column3: Step into the world of refined relaxation with the Liana Upholstered Fabric Sofa, a stylish centerpiece that combines comfort with a chic, casual aesthetic. Embodying a retro-modern look, the Liana 3 Seater Sofa features dense foam padding encased in fabric upholstery, perfect for sinking into after a long day. Enhancing the soft couch’s allure, subtly tufted seats blend with a neatly stitched grid pattern that extends into the gently curved armrests and backrests, imparting a touch of geometric flair. Its low profile and deep seating are thoughtfully designed to cater to contemporary aesthetics while providing ample space to relax. Durably constructed and supported by solid wood bun feet with non-marking floor glides, the Liana Upholstered Sofa Couch stands strong, ready to support countless lounge times. Perfectly at home in a chic modern living room or a mid-century modern lounge, the Liana Deep Seat Sofa beckons you to unwind in style. Weight Capacity: 800 lbs.
column4:
Welsh quilters have stitched thick layers of wool and cotton into bold geometric patterns for generations, and Lampeter, in Ceredigion, keeps one of the finest collections of their work. The same idea, soft layers held in shape by neat lines of stitching, gives this sofa its character.

The seat is biscuit-tufted, stitched down into a grid of shallow squares, and the stitched lines carry on up the rounded arms and across the back. Dense foam gives the deep seat a soft, supportive feel, and low, round bun feet of solid wood lift it on glides that will not mark the floor. It seats three, with a sturdy build made for years of family evenings.

Its low, deep seat makes it the sofa for a family room or a den where everyone wants to put their feet up. Set it in a mid-century living room with a round coffee table, or along the wall of a quiet reading room. Add a jute rug, linen cushions and a ceramic table lamp.

column3: Glamour radiates from the organic linear design of the Sanguine Performance Velvet Sofa. Relax and follow the interior vertical channel tufting for a streamlined effect that adds retro modern glamour to your living room, lounge room, or home office. Soft, stain-resistant performance velvet upholstery creates a luxurious tactile experience while dense foam padding with individually wrapped spring coil system provides ultimate comfort and support. Sanguine’s palatial accents and premium comfort rest securely on a gold stainless steel base that complements any contemporary modern home or apartment. Maximum weight capacity: 900 lbs.
column4:
Stockholm's Concert Hall opened in 1926 in the Norrmalm district and became a landmark of the style English writers called Swedish Grace: classical order pared back until it looked new. It was elegance without fuss, and the same instinct runs through this sofa.

Its outline is a single crisp box, the arms rising straight to the height of the back. Every inside surface is channel tufted, stitched into deep vertical ribs that run like the fluting on a column. Dense foam sits over individually wrapped springs, the velvet is a performance fabric that shrugs off spills, and the whole sofa floats on a recessed plinth of gold-finish stainless steel. It is built for a full row of guests.

Give it the main wall of a living room, facing a pair of chairs across a round marble coffee table, or set it in a home office for an afternoon with a book. Velvet and gold suit black lacquer and big abstract canvases; add a mohair throw and a stack of art books.

In early twentieth-century Stockholm apartments, the best seat in the house was the armchair drawn up to the tiled stove, the tall glazed heater that warmed Swedish rooms for generations. A good chair there was square, solid and deeply upholstered, built for a long winter evening.

This one keeps that solid footprint and dresses it up. Its arms and back form one even, boxy frame, and the inside is channel tufted into upright ribs of velvet, with a seat tufted to match. The padding is dense foam over individually wrapped springs, the performance velvet is chosen to resist stains, and a band of gold-finish stainless steel lifts the chair just clear of the floor. It is built to be sat in every day.

Put it in a bedroom corner with a floor lamp and a side table for the book you are halfway through, or in an entryway to greet guests. In a living room it partners almost any sofa. Drape a sheepskin over one arm and set a tall plant beside it.

A left-arm chair, two armless chairs and a right-arm chair join into a long four-seat sofa, and two square ottomans complete it, one at each end, so two people can stretch out at once. The oldest apartment buildings in Stockholm's old town were built around narrow, winding stone stairwells, and anyone who has carried a sofa up one knows why furniture in separate parts makes sense. A sofa that arrives as three seats goes up any stair, then becomes one piece in the room.

This one is three pieces, a left-arm chair, an armless centre seat and a right-arm chair, which lock together into a squared three-seat sofa. The arms stand level with the back, and the inside is stitched into deep vertical channels of velvet for a tailored, ribbed look. Dense foam and individually wrapped springs fill a wood and plywood frame, the performance velvet resists everyday stains, and a gold-finish stainless steel plinth runs beneath. It is sturdy enough for everyday family use.

It suits a city apartment, a study or a guest room where space is tight, and it can be rearranged or added to later. Pair it with a round coffee table, a slim floor lamp and a tall fiddle-leaf fig.

column3: Settle into sculptural comfort with the Hawken Boucle Fabric Upholstered Sofa. Designed with bold curves and oversized proportions, this three-seater couch offers a wide, inviting seat and gently sloped armrests for a cozy reading or relaxation experience. Upholstered in soft brushed boucle fabric, Hawken adds depth and visual warmth to any space—from living room to apartment to office lounge. The sturdy solid wood legs complement the textured boucle upholstery with natural warmth and mid-century charm. With a supportive foam-padded seat, plush back cushions, and zigzag spring suspension, this modern sofa delivers everyday comfort with timeless style. Assembly required. Weight Capacity: 500 lbs.
column4:
Langholm, in the Scottish Borders, grew up around its woollen mills, and the Borders have long woven cloth with a nubbly, hand-friendly texture. Bouclé belongs to that family of cloths: the name is French for curled, after the little loops in the yarn that give the surface its soft, pebbled feel.

This sofa wraps a clean, squared frame in brushed bouclé and sets it on solid wood legs that rise up the front of each arm like a slim timber edging. The arms slope gently, the seat is wide enough for three, and zigzag springs beneath a foam-padded seat keep it supportive through years of evenings. Three plush cushions line the back, and the build is made for daily family use.

Set it facing the fire with a wool throw and a novel on the arm, or let it anchor a studio apartment or a home office lounge on its own. Pair it with a round wooden coffee table, a jute rug and linen cushions in warm stone and rust.

column4:
Nests of small tables became a fixture of Georgian drawing rooms in Britain and Ireland in the late eighteenth century: graduated sets that tucked one beneath the next and came out when company called. The idea still earns its keep wherever floor space is precious.

These are a pair of round drums in two sizes, the larger one taller and broader, each wrapped in wood veneer with the grain running from top to bottom. Push them together in front of a sofa as one coffee table, then draw the smaller one out beside an armchair when guests need somewhere for a glass. In a bedroom they make low bedside drums. Dress the larger with tulips and a few art books. This listing is for a set of two tables.

Mérida, in western Spain, was founded by the Romans as Augusta Emerita, and its great theatre still stands, a stage backed by tiers of columns. The Romans were also the first great builders in concrete, and something of that weight and calm carries into this table.

An oval top with softly rounded ends rests on two pedestals, each a trefoil, meaning three rounded columns gathered into one, so the base reads like a pair of carved stone feet. On the coast of County Clare, Liscannor flagstone has been cut for floors, hearths and garden paths for generations, its surface marked with the trails of sea creatures from long ago. A slab resting on two uprights is among the oldest forms of furniture there is.

This table keeps that slab-and-upright shape: a thick rectangular top whose edges are rounded over, a profile known as bullnose, set on two broad panel legs. It is built from MDF and hardwood under a textured cement finish, mottled like weathered stone. Levelling feet underneath keep it steady on an uneven floor without marking it, and it needs some assembly.

Set it in front of a low sofa in a calm living room, with a heavy art book, a smooth river stone and a single branch in a jug. It also anchors a home office lounge. Pair it with bouclé chairs, a pale wool rug and warm wood for a quiet, coastal feel.

Cement finish
Wipe with a soft cloth, dry or barely damp, and dry straight after. Use coasters under glasses and mats under hot dishes, and wipe up spills straight away, especially wine, coffee, citrus and oil, which can mark the textured surface. Avoid abrasive, acidic or harsh cleaners and scouring pads.

column3: The Annette Side Table stands on a wide cylindrical base of powder-coated steel, with a narrower column recessed beneath the round top. The industrial metal base sits flat and steady on the floor. Because the base sits at the center, the edge of the 22-inch top stays open all the way around, and the table pulls in flush against the arm of a sofa. The top is oak veneer over a durable wood core base, finished in lacquer that wipes clean with a damp cloth. Arrives fully assembled. Weight capacity 99 lb.
column4:
Andalusian houses keep their small tables close to hand, a round top by a favourite chair for a glass of sherry, a lamp and the book of the moment. This one follows the same instinct, with a single solid support that keeps clear of chair arms and knees.

Its round top is wood veneer over a sturdy wood core, lacquered so a damp cloth is all it needs, and it stands on a recessed metal column set into a wide drum of powder-coated steel in a burnished metallic tone. The broad drum keeps it steady, and the overhanging top lets it tuck in tight beside a sofa. It is strong enough for a lamp and a pile of books, and it arrives fully assembled.

Put it at the end of a sofa with a reading lamp and a glass of water, or beside a velvet armchair in a wood-panelled study. It works as a bedside table too. Rust, olive and deep green textiles suit the dark wood and warm metal.

column3: Blending natural textures with modern versatility, the Lazaro Side Table is a stylish and functional accent piece for any space. This round rattan side table features an intricate handwoven base with a sculptural hourglass silhouette, adding a touch of organic beauty to boho, coastal, or eclectic interiors. The metal tabletop has a warm finish with a raised lip, offering both style and practicality for holding drinks, books, or decorative pieces. Designed with convenience in mind, the removable tray top on this versatile end table allows for easy serving or styling. Whether used as a bedside table, accent table, or indoor plant stand, this woven rattan table makes a statement while keeping your space effortlessly chic. Weight Capacity: 75 lbs.
column4:
On the Costa Blanca, not far from Altea, the village of Gata de Gorgos has woven baskets, chairs and hampers by hand for generations, and Mediterranean Spain still keeps woven furniture on its terraces and in its cool, shaded rooms. Woven pieces are light to move and easy on the eye.

This small table is hand-woven rattan shaped into an hourglass, flaring out at the foot and again beneath the top, so it looks almost turned. On top sits a round metal tray in a warm gold tone, its rim raised so a glass or cup stays put. The tray lifts away for carrying drinks or snacks to the table, and the woven base is firm underfoot.

Stand it beside a linen sofa with a carafe of water and a dish of oranges, or at a bedside with a lamp and a book. It makes a pretty plant stand in a sunroom and suits a beach house or a coastal living room. White walls, jute and pale wood keep it fresh.

column3: Revitalize your space with the classic-meets-modern design of the Tarin Round Side Table. Featuring a solid marble top that exudes elegance while resting on sturdy acacia wood legs, this marble round table complements a variety of interiors from mid-century modern to minimalist. The accent table's distinctive base highlights the natural beauty of wood, with its crossbeam-style legs featuring wide, flat ends that extend outward for a sturdy and grounded look. Perfect as a marble end table for the living room or an accent table in the bedroom, Tarin pairs natural elements with a chic, updated look. Designed for versatility, it also works beautifully as a modern drink table, side cocktail table, or even a marble plant table. However you choose to use it, Tarin comes with adjustable floor protectors for added stability while safeguarding your floors from scratches. Assembly required. Weight Capacity: 33 lbs.
column4:
Around Estremoz, in Portugal's Alentejo, marble has been quarried since Roman times, and the pale stone turns up everywhere from palace floors to the doorsteps of whitewashed village houses. A disc of marble on a simple wooden stand is a very old and very good pairing.

Here the stand is two flat hardwood slabs slotted together in a cross, their broad, square-cut ends reaching out to the floor so the table stands firm. The round top is solid marble, white with soft grey veining, every one a little different. Adjustable pads under the feet protect the floor and steady it on uneven boards. It needs some assembly.

Set it beside an armchair for a morning cup of coffee, at the end of a sofa as a drink table, or by the bed with a lamp. It makes a handsome stand for a potted fern or an orchid. Natural wood and pale stone sit well with linen, cane and terracotta.

Marble top
Marble is porous, so wipe up spills straight away, especially wine, coffee, citrus and oil, and use coasters under glasses and hot dishes. Clean with a soft cloth and a little mild soap in water, then dry. Avoid acidic or abrasive cleaners, which can etch or dull the stone.

Wood base
Dust with a soft, dry cloth, and wipe occasionally with a barely damp one, drying straight after. Keep out of direct sun and away from radiators and heat vents to protect the wood.

column3: Enhance your living area with the Caspian Side Table, an ideal modern accent table for daily convenience and decorative flair. This elegant round end table, perfect for any living room, bedroom, or lounge area, features a unique trefoil-shaped pedestal base, adding a contemporary touch to your home or apartment. Crafted from MDF with a stylish concrete overlay, this piece serves well as a compact side table for small spaces or as a chic hallway table. The Caspian Living Room Side Table, balancing durability with sleek design, includes felt pads for floor protection. Weight Limit: 198 lbs.
column4:
The Roman builders who raised Mérida in western Spain understood that a column could be both a support and an ornament. This small table takes that old idea indoors and sets it beside a chair.

A deep, bowl-like top crowns a trefoil pedestal, three rounded columns gathered together, so the piece reads like a short classical pillar. It is MDF, a dense engineered board, with a concrete overlay for a quiet mineral texture, and felt pads underneath protect the floor. It is sturdy enough for a heavy lamp or a stack of books.

Put one beside the sofa for a glass and a paperback, at a bedside, or in a hallway to hold keys and a small vase. It also fits a narrow corner where a four-legged table would crowd the floor. A trailing plant or a pair of brass candlesticks looks good on its round top.
